content:
OPERATIONAL — comms-dispatcher 403-loop incident and fix (2026-05-09 to 2026-05-15). Failure: dispatcher process held the pre-rotation bridge token in memory from before the 2026-05-09 token rotation. bridge_config.py reads ~/.config/sovereign-bridge.env only at process start. After rotation, the live process kept hitting HTTP 403 Forbidden on every poll. Throttled. Eventually launchd gave up restarting (plist KeepAlive=true with ThrottleInterval=30s).

Dormant period: 2026-05-09 22:51 (last 403) through 2026-05-15 10:08 (fresh process). Approximately 5.5 days unloaded. Last successful comms post 2026-05-08T07:17.

Fix: launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.templetwo.comms-dispatcher.plist. Fresh process reads current token from env file. First post-restart request returned HTTP 200 OK. Process pid 10682, on commit 87b0ccf (self-filter version).

Class: stale-in-memory-token-survives-rotation. Not specific to comms_dispatcher — any persistent daemon that caches secrets at process start has this exposure. Counter-pattern: SIGHUP handler that re-reads config, or shorter process lifetime by design.

This incident is the validating evidence in the DISPATCHER_REIMAGINE.md RFC for why the Sonnet replacement needs explicit cost-and-halt circuits surfacing failures upstream, not silent 403 loops absorbed by daemon restart logic.
